title: Easy Bhangra Dance Tutorial || Candlelight || Top 3 Beginner Bhangra Steps || BHANGRAlicious

method.teacher_system: The teacher greets the learners and outlines the steps to be taught, then breaks down three beginner Bhangra steps one by one—focusing on feet first, then arms and styling. Finally, she combines all three steps into a short choreographed routine practiced both with and without music.
method.signature: She refers to shoulder movement and upper body posture as 'the party in the shoulders', adding personality and distinct imagery to the instruction.

practices.what: The teacher breaks down the first step, Dhamaal, starting with the leg movements and posture.
The teacher adds arm positioning and shoulder bouncing to the previously learned leg movement of Dhamaal.
The teacher has learners practice 8 counts of Dhamaal along with music.
The teacher breaks down the second step, Bedi, focusing on side-to-side foot taps and minor squats.
The teacher adds circular arm movements and a graceful clapping motion to the Bedi step.
The teacher has learners practice 8 counts of Bedi along with music.
The teacher breaks down the third step, Punjab, an alternate hop and cross-tap footwork.
The teacher adds overhead arm placement and shoulder bouncing to the Punjab step.
The teacher has learners practice the Punjab step along with music.
The teacher combines all three learned steps into a full choreography sequence practiced across counts.

adaptations.difficulty: Keeping balance while lifting the leg high
adaptations.adjustment: Go higher if you can keep your balance, keeping the knee bent

adaptations.difficulty: Standing with feet wider than shoulder width
adaptations.adjustment: Stand almost in a little squat with spine relatively straight

adaptations.difficulty: Doing the physical clap with hands
adaptations.adjustment: Pretend you are clapping and do not actually do the clap for a more graceful look
Tilt slightly towards the stepping side to keep your balance

beliefs.belief: Anyone can learn these top beginner Bhangra steps to jam to their favorite songs.

moments.says: The teacher introduces herself warmly as Bhangralicious and welcomes the viewer to learn three beginner Bhangra steps.
The teacher explains the first step called Dhamaal by breaking down the leg placement and posture first.
The teacher smiles and reassures the learner that the first step was really nice and easy.
The teacher introduces the second step called Bedi and explains foot positioning and wider stance.
The teacher praises the learner for nicely completing the second step practice.
The teacher introduces the third and final step called Punjab, detailing the leg crossover movement.
The teacher encourages the learner to put all three steps together into a quick choreography routine.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable, energized, and ready to dance Bhangra with confidence.

struggles.theme: Trying to coordinate arms with legs is hard
Easy to watch but hard to execute

clicked.theme: Easy to follow tutorials and clear breakdown
Detailed explanation of step names and body structure

requests.theme: Requests for more practice or personal lessons

meant.theme: Brings joy, puts learners in a great mood, and connects them to Punjabi culture

method.limits: The video does not show partner interactions or full group formations, and only upper-body and lower-body close-ups are highlighted via split screen.
